system.description:
Purification embodies the removal of that which has corrupted something from its proper state: poison from blood, disease from flesh, curses from souls and desecration from sacred places. It is usually represented as white flame, flowing water or a silver vessel from which darkness is being washed away.
Its better traditions are careful to distinguish corruption from difference. A person, race, culture or belief is not impure merely because it is unfamiliar. Purification concerns harmful intrusion and supernatural corruption, not persecution disguised as holiness.

Edicts: Cleanse disease, poison, curses and supernatural corruption. Restore desecrated sacred places. Destroy dangerous spiritual contamination. Keep medical, funerary and ritual practices clean. Identify corruption accurately before attempting to purge it.

Anathema: Deliberately spread disease, poison or supernatural corruption. Desecrate something sacred merely to demonstrate power. Describe an innocent people as corruption in order to justify persecution. Preserve a dangerous contaminating influence when you could safely remove it.

Suggested Ethics: Benevolence, Discipline, Justice

Class Skill: Perception

Specialist Spells: Protective Ward (1), Radiant Aegis (1), Spoil the Profane (1), Wash Away Sin (1), Purge the Unlife (7), Renewal's Touch (7), Revealing Glance (7), Searing Burst (7)

Bonus Spells: Purify (2); Restore Senses (4); Remove Disease (6); Remove Curse (8)

Favoured Weapon: Flail

Pillars of Faith, Chapter 7. Add it from the sheet's Divine Aspect slot: the class skill and favoured weapon apply, the bonus spells arrive at their levels, and Use chooses the specialist spell (PP 1 for a Grimward or Cleric).
